history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the documented Narvadeshwar (Narbadeshwar) Temple is NOT in Shimla — it stands at Sujanpur Tira, Hamirpur district, roughly 100+ km from Shimla; the CSV town is wrong. It was built in 1802 by Maharani Prasanni Devi, wife of Maharaja Sansar Chand Katoch of Kangra, in Panchayatan (Bhitti) style on open ground near the Beas river. Its walls carry renowned Kangra-style murals depicting scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavata Purana plus animals and birds. Smaller shrines of Surya, Durga, Ganesha, Lakshmi-Narayana and Mahishasura Mardini surround the main shrine. Low-quality SEO pages mix this temple up with a claimed shrine at Kundbhard village in the lower Shimla hills — unverified; the Sujanpur Tira identity is the sourced one.

name: Narvadeshwar Temple
town_description: Sujanpur Tira is a historic town in Hamirpur district, Himachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Beas river. It was a stronghold of the Katoch rulers of Kangra, whose fort ruins still stand on the hill above the town. Today it is a quiet pilgrimage and heritage stop on the road between Hamirpur and Kangra.

travel.railway: No railhead at Hamirpur; nearest stations Una or Amb Andaura, ~55-60 km (verify)
travel.road: On SH-39, ~24 km from Hamirpur town; connected by bus and taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (avoid heavy monsoon July-August)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Around 8:00 AM-6:00 PM (verify); visitors report no strict fixed timings
